title: Probability: Events, Axioms and the Addition Rule
seo_title: Probability Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 14)
standard_text: Events: occurrence of events, 'not', 'and' and 'or' events, exhaustive events, mutually exclusive events; axiomatic (set theoretic) probability, connections with other theories studied in earlier classes; probability of an event, probability of 'not', 'and' and 'or' events (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Probability worksheet (NCERT Chapter 14): sample spaces, coins, dice and cards, complementary and mutually exclusive events, axioms and P(A ∪ B). 100 questions with answers.
key_big: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
body_html:
How it works

  • The sample space S is the set of all outcomes. An event is a subset of S.
  • Axioms: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1, P(S) = 1, and probabilities of outcomes add up to 1.
  • A and B are mutually exclusive if A ∩ B = φ; then P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
  • In general P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B), and P(A′) = 1 − P(A).
Example

3 coins are tossed. Find P(at least one head).

8 outcomes; only TTT has no head

1 − 1/8

Answer: 7/8

Common mistakes

  • Adding P(A) + P(B) when A and B overlap.
  • Taking 6 outcomes for 3 coins (there are 8).
  • Treating 'at least one' as 'exactly one'.
